rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Barbeyrac's note 3 on II.3.23 makes the same point about Roman usage, and Vattel's footnote repeats its Cicero quotation (De off. III.5, 'natura, id est, jure gentium'), which none of the other sources here contains.

rejudge.label: verbatim
rejudge.reason: Vattel copies Barbeyrac's French of Hobbes, De cive XIV.4, word for word, and his footnote names this paragraph.

rejudge.label: verbatim
rejudge.reason: Vattel continues the same quotation of Hobbes in Barbeyrac's French almost word for word, leaving out only 'des Devoirs'.

rejudge.label: open disagreement
rejudge.reason: Vattel says Hobbes was wrong that natural law and the law of nations have 'précisément les mêmes' maxims, then adds that Pufendorf subscribes to this view.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: Vattel's footnote says he uses Barbeyrac's translation in Pufendorf II.3.23, where this Hobbes passage stands.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel quotes Barbeyrac's note 2 on Buddeus almost word for word, putting 'la chose' for 'la coûtume', and cites the note itself.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: Vattel's note (i) cites note 2 on Pufendorf II.3.23 for the Buddeus remark.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The wording translates Wolff, Jus gentium Prol. §3 ('Jus Gentium originarie non est nisi Jus naturae ad Gentes applicatum'), and the Hobbes passage in Pufendorf only states the same idea.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Barbeyrac's note 2, which Vattel quotes and cites in his preface, has the same rule: nations are presumed to follow a custom unless they have expressly declared they will not, and Wolff's Prol. §24 lacks it.

rejudge.label: verbatim
rejudge.reason: The nine words are identical but idiomatic, and the note is about private war; Vattel's point that a subject people is no longer a state is broader and only overlaps.

rejudge.label: verbatim
rejudge.reason: Both quote the 1667 Traité des droits de la Reine, but Vattel cites a different edition and page (II partie p. 191, not Barbeyrac's p. 310) and lacks Barbeyrac's 'donc' and 'mais', so he probably quoted the treatise directly.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Pufendorf VIII.1.6 gives the same sequence: in doubtful cases subjects should presume the order just, not examine it, and the fault falls wholly on the sovereign.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows the two cases of Barbeyrac's note (on II.5.5, not II.4.5): resist a prince who attacks deliberately, but spare one not master of himself even at the cost of one's own life, as with Charles VI.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Avoiding the troubles of repeated elections is the stock reason for hereditary monarchy, given in the same words in Barbeyrac's preface to Grotius, and nothing ties Vattel's sentence to this one.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel poses Pufendorf's question in his wording ('on demande ... deux ou plusieurs prétendans à la couronne') and names Pufendorf later in the paragraph.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: Vattel names Pufendorf (with Grotius) as denying that the people's decision is a juridical sentence, which this sentence of VII.7.15 states.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: Vattel names Pufendorf for the view that such disputes cannot be decided with authority by juridical sentence, as this sentence says.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: Vattel names Pufendorf for the view that the people's verdict is no juridical sentence, which Pufendorf calls a simple approbation here.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The rule is in the same Barbeyrac wording in Grotius II.7.16, which Pufendorf copies, and Grotius's reason (certainty in the succession) is closer to Vattel's, so nothing points to Pufendorf.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Pufendorf and Barbeyrac's note on Grotius I.3.15 both say a power to name a successor comes from the people's grant, and Vattel reframes 'patrimonial' kingdoms in his own way.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Pufendorf, restating Grotius II.6.4, gives the founders' intention not to be placed under foreign rule as the bar on alienation, and Vattel's wording ('ont formé ... sont entrés', 'joug étranger') is closer to Pufendorf's than to Grotius's.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Wolff, Jus gentium §58 (free to buy or not, 'ab hoc potius quam ab alio'; no right to sell to a nation unwilling to buy), and Pufendorf, restating Grotius, only states the same doctrine.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The point that excluded nations cannot complain, not even of a refused office of humanity, is Wolff, Jus gentium §59, and Pufendorf only has the general idea.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Justifying tolls by the cost of building and maintaining works is common doctrine (Grotius II.2.14; Wolff, Jus gentium §§119, 214, whose idea that those who share the benefit should pay is closer to Vattel).

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: That overvalued coin is useless with foreigners is a commonplace (also in Pufendorf's Devoirs), and Vattel's paragraph rests on Boizard, whom he cites, and on Wolff's intrinsic and extrinsic value.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same Erastian argument (take religion and teaching from the sovereign and troubles follow), but it is a stock ius circa sacra commonplace (Hobbes, Burlamaqui) and Vattel's recapitulation shares only the 'ôter au souverain' turn.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Barbeyrac's Lockean note states the same transfer of the natural right to punish, but Vattel's sequence (natural right grounded on security, correction and example, transfer to society, society as moral person punishing public crimes) follows Wolff, Inst. §§ 93, 1028-1030.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same specific argument on duels: while the honour custom stands, the magistrate cannot justly punish the man who defends his reputation by it; Pufendorf II.5.12 has it and Wolff does not.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same specific remedy from Pufendorf II.5.12: treat the insulted man who fights leniently and punish the insulter very severely.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same presumption, framed as in Pufendorf as the individual's tacit engagement on entering society and tied to his own affairs; Vattel narrows it to temporary absence, and I.222 goes on to follow the same Pufendorf paragraph.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same survey of how states' laws differ on leaving, with the phrase 'sans (une) permission expresse du souverain' taken from Pufendorf VIII.11.2.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Grotius II.5.25 states the same point (the state keeps no jurisdiction over those it banishes) and Pufendorf repeats it; the first half of Vattel's sentence (banished only from that state's lands) follows Wolff JG § 147, as the whole unit follows Wolff §§ 145-147.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's definition of eminent domain follows Wolff (Inst. § 1065, Jus nat. VIII § 111) almost word for word; Pufendorf only states that it applies in necessity.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's sentence, with its 'unless expressly reserved' clause, translates Wolff, Jus nat. VIII § 112; Pufendorf only says that conferring sovereignty conveys what the state needs.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The duty to compensate is common doctrine, and Vattel's wording 'dédommagé des deniers publics' comes from Grotius III.20.7 (and Wolff, Jus nat. VIII § 119, 'ex aerario publico'), not from Pufendorf.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Bearing burdens in proportion is a stock equity maxim, also in Grotius III.20.7-8; Vattel's wording and his jettison analogy do not follow Pufendorf.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Gradual alluvion going to the owner of the bank is a Roman-law commonplace, and Vattel's frame (arcifinious territory, right of alluvion) follows Wolff JG §§ 108-109; the wording is not close to Pufendorf's.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Avulsion leaving the torn-off land with its first owner is a Roman-law commonplace (Inst. 2.1.21) and nothing ties Vattel's wording to Pufendorf.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's presumption and its reason ('rien n'est plus naturel') follow Wolff JG § 109 and Grotius II.3.17; Pufendorf has only a parenthetical 'ce que l'on présume dans un doute'.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Wolff JG § 106 lists the same cases (river common, divided at the middle, or held by one nation), and the main clause follows Wolff § 109; Pufendorf's list has 'vacante', not 'commun'.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's list follows Wolff JG § 120 ('conchas, gemmas et alicubi succinum': shells, pearls, amber), not Pufendorf's pearls, coral and amber.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Salt-making is in Wolff JG § 120's list, in the same order as Vattel's sentence; the echo of Pufendorf's 'sert encore à faire du sel' is too slight to show a borrowing.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's sentence follows Wolff JG § 121 (navigation and fishing harm no one, hence inexhaustible use); Pufendorf only calls navigation innocent.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The rule that things of inexhaustible use cannot be appropriated is common to Grotius II.2.3, Pufendorf and Wolff JG § 121, and Vattel's phrasing as a rule about the right to appropriate follows Wolff.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Pufendorf IV.5.4's specific sequence: inexhaustible things stay common, the earth was divided because a large population could not live on it without cultivation, and that reason does not apply to the ocean.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Grotius II.2.3 makes the same claim (the cause for leaving community does not apply to the sea); IV.5.9 states it only in general, and the closer Pufendorf wording is in IV.5.4 ('raison particulière qui n'a point de lieu à l'égard de l'Océan').

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Wolff JG § 128 (fishing and collecting what grows in the sea near coasts is not inexhaustible); Pufendorf's sentence is more general.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same concession and rhetorical question as Pufendorf IV.5.7 (fish seem more plentiful, yet coastal people may keep a fruitful fishery for themselves); Wolff § 128 lacks it, but the wording differs too much for close paraphrase.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel renders Wolff JG § 128 ('intersit accolarum, ne cuilibet ibidem cum armatis navibus versari liceat') nearly word for word; Pufendorf only states the same danger from foreign warships.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: Vattel names Bodin, not Pufendorf or Barbeyrac, so this is not a citation; his details (thirty leagues, Rép. I.10) come from the French Bodin, not Barbeyrac's sixty miles and Lib. I cap. ult.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's double limit (as far as safety requires and as far as the state can enforce it) and its justification follow Wolff JG §127-128 (quousque dominium tueri possunt; absurd to claim a right one cannot defend); Pufendorf states only the rampart criterion.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The cannon-shot rule was common doctrine by 1758 (Bynkershoek); Barbeyrac's note states it, but no wording or argument ties Vattel to it, and Vattel's neutral-prize corollary comes from Bynkershoek, not Barbeyrac.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Extending coastal dominion to bays and straits follows Wolff JG §128 ('idem intelligitur de sinibus et fretis') and Grotius II.3.8; Pufendorf's sentence states the same doctrine (his nearby 'sur tout des Rades' may echo, but nothing decisive).

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Only 'modique' is shared: Pufendorf's clause restrains an odious strait toll while Vattel justifies one; Vattel's specific debt to this paragraph is the list of services (row 54).

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's services justifying the strait toll (clearing pirates, maintaining fanaux and balises) use Pufendorf's words ('entretenir des Fanaux', 'Balises'), not Grotius's 'feux allumez', and Wolff has no parallel; but the list is reordered and cut down, so loose rather than close.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's sequence (anyone may renounce his right, so a nation may covenant to restrict its trade in favour of another or not to trade with a given country) translates Wolff JG §202-203; Pufendorf gives the same maxim in a monopoly context with a different sentence structure.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Stock definition of full ownership as the exclusive right to dispose at will; Vattel's deduction (else I could not dispose freely) is Wolffian, and nothing ties it to Pufendorf.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: A shared Tacitus saying: Vattel translates the Latin himself (his note quotes Tacitus), and his comment that the remonstrance was misapplied because the land had a use follows Grotius II.2.17, while Pufendorf sides with the Ansibarii.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The necessity right is common doctrine; Vattel's national version (forced sale at a fair price, revival of primitive community) follows Wolff JG §340-342 and Inst. §304, and Pufendorf's rhetorical question shares only the general point.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The proviso that the owner not be in the same necessity is Grotius's standard restriction (II.2.8), repeated by Pufendorf; Vattel's ships, wagons, horses and foreigners' labour come from Wolff JG §342.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's argument (a people of men cannot conserve itself, so may obtain wives and use force if refused, Sabines) follows Wolff JG §341, which he cites; Pufendorf's Florus point (one generation) is the same commonplace.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Both say women must not be forced into marriage, but Pufendorf addresses parents refusing suitors; Vattel's limit on a nation's right of force is his own correction of Wolff §341, and the shared point is general.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's sentence follows Grotius II.2.12 directly (including 'c'est-à-dire ... boire & puiser'); Pufendorf only reports Grotius's formula and then questions it.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Demanding guarantees for a dangerous passage is common doctrine (Grotius II.2.13, Wolff JG §356, §698); Vattel's framing (passage owed only while harmless) is Wolff's, and Pufendorf only reports others' view.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Tolls as compensation for upkeep of roads and canals are a stock justification (Grotius II.2.14 'pour s'en dédommager', Wolff JG §119); Vattel refers back to his own I.103.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Probus and Valens together, with Gepids, Vandals and Goths, and the same three references (Vopiscus c. 18, Ammianus 31, Socrates IV.28) come from Pufendorf III.3.10 and its margins, which Grotius and Wolff lack; Vattel compresses two narratives into one sentence.

rejudge.label: verbatim
rejudge.reason: Vattel's note reproduces Pufendorf's margin references (f), (g), (h) for Probus and Valens in the same order.

rejudge.label: verbatim
rejudge.reason: Same French rendering of Caesar's reply to the Tencteri and Usipetes, word for word from Barbeyrac's Pufendorf III.3.10 (not in Grotius).

rejudge.label: verbatim
rejudge.reason: The same Latin from Barbeyrac's note 8, which goes with the French Vattel copies from the same paragraph.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel adopts the thesis that Pufendorf only reports from Grotius II.2.22 and then rejects; his wording and list of acts follow Grotius and Wolff JG §348.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's distinction for rights granted to particular nations follows Wolff JG §349 ('per modum beneficii') and Grotius II.2.23; the partial match with Pufendorf's favour/convention/promise triad is suggestive, but Pufendorf uses it to reject Grotius's thesis.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Stock Roman-law definition: Vattel names Modestinus and translates the Digest Latin (continuationem, lege definiti) more closely than Pufendorf's French, which gives the same law.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Both note that French 'prescription' covers both terms and then choose to use it generally; this is Barbeyrac's note to Pufendorf IV.12.1, a chapter Vattel cites in the next section.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The quoted clause concerns renunciation by a positive act (dealing with the possessor as owner); presumed abandonment from long neglect is Grotius's doctrine (II.4.5), reported in this §, and Vattel's 'présomption absolue juris et de jure' is Wolff Inst. §462.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: Vattel's note cites Pufendorf IV.12, the chapter on prescription.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: Vattel's note to II.141 names Pufendorf IV.12, the chapter on prescription, for the claim that prescription is of natural law; §7 is where Pufendorf discusses that question.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Both ground prescription on the peace of mankind, but Vattel's a fortiori point (states' quarrels end in bloody wars, no peace if old claims revive) is closer to Grotius II.4.1; Pufendorf IV.12.9 only states the general ground.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's sentence is the conclusion of Wolff JG §359 (fear of a stronger power, prescription from silence hard between nations; 'Personne n'ignore' = 'Qui non ignorat'); Pufendorf IV.12.8 only states that long silence does not always prove abandonment.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Barbeyrac's note grounds prescription on the end of property rather than presumed abandonment and calls the former owner's loss a misfortune he must accept; Vattel makes the same move in II.149 with the same idea, absent from Wolff and Grotius.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's maxim and its sequel (the acceptor need not judge, nations have no superior) translate Wolff JG §407 ('omnia probe expenderit... antequam promittat'); Pufendorf V.3.9 says it of commercial bargains and still allows rescission for considerable lesion.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Nullity of engagements to unlawful things for want of moral power is common doctrine already in Grotius II.11.8 (and II.16.26 for the wording 'personne ne pouvant s'engager'); nothing ties Vattel to Pufendorf III.7.6.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's preference for the ally with the just cause, whether at war with another ally or a third state, follows Grotius II.15.13; Pufendorf VIII.6.14 only says one is not bound to aid an ally in an unjust war.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Beyond Grotius II.15.5 (which Vattel cites), Vattel follows Pufendorf's 'Parmi les Anciens... absolument nécessaires' and answers his claim that civilized peoples need no such treaties ('utiles même entre les nations les plus policées').

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's tacit exception and grain-in-famine example come from Wolff JG §388; Pufendorf VIII.9.5 states a looser version of the same exception (interests of one's kingdom).

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's first clause translates Wolff JG §398 ('eadem aut aequivalentia non promittuntur') and the dignity criterion is in Grotius I.3.21; Pufendorf's two-pronged definition is a plausible but not demonstrable model, and Vattel splits it into treaty versus alliance.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The two-fold division by which side bears the inequality is Grotius II.15.7 (also Wolff §398); Vattel's 'puissance inférieure' is closer to Grotius's 'du côté de l'inférieure' than to Pufendorf's 'Allié inférieur en dignité'.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's 'secours gratuits, ou plus grands' renders Wolff JG §398 ('vel gratuitas, vel majores'); Pufendorf VIII.9.4 repeats Grotius II.15.7 on the same point.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's list follows the order of Wolff JG §398 and takes 'maintenir & respecter sa majesté' verbatim from Grotius II.15.7, which Pufendorf lacks; Pufendorf only repeats Grotius's list.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's wording ('promirent... de ne faire la guerre à personne sans le consentement du peuple Romain', 'dépendans des Romains') is Barbeyrac's Grotius II.15.7.5; Pufendorf has the same example in other words.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel copies Grotius II.16.16.3 almost verbatim, Pedius and Ulpian included; Pufendorf VIII.9.6 states the same Digest rule in different words.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Besides Wolff §416 (change of form), Vattel's 'Toute alliance faite par une république est réelle de sa nature', the death of the magistrates and 'en monarchie' match Pufendorf's sentence more closely than Grotius's 'Tout Traité'.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's exception ('Il faut excepter', made 'dans la vue de' preserving the free government, alliance ends when one of the two changes) follows Pufendorf's wording and his explicit consequence more closely than Grotius II.16.16.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The rule is Grotius II.16.16.4, which Pufendorf reports as Grotius's; Vattel's reason (duration cannot depend on the contractants' lives) follows Wolff JG §417.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Grotius II.16.16.4 has the same clause and conclusion ('pour lui & ses Successeurs... on voit assez par là, que le Traité est réel'); Pufendorf merely reports Grotius's list.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The rule is Grotius II.16.16.4 ('clause expresse, qui porte que le Traité est fait... pour le bien du Roiaume') reported by Pufendorf, and Vattel's reasoning about the contractants' lives follows Wolff JG §418.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's 'En cas de doute' frame follows Wolff JG §420 and his 'roule sur des choses favorables' matches Barbeyrac's Grotius II.16.16.6, which Pufendorf only reports.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's definition translates Wolff JG §420 ('ad communem utilitatem spectant & utrique parti aequaliter consulunt'); Pufendorf V.12.12 (after Grotius II.16.10) gives the criteria in reverse order and speaks of public utility.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's 'chargent une partie seule, ou... beaucoup plus que l'autre' renders Wolff JG §420 ('partem alteram tantum onerant, aut plus onerant'); Pufendorf V.12.12 and Grotius II.16.10 give the same stock definition.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel names Grotius and copies Barbeyrac's Grotius II.16.16.6 ('ont quelque chose qui approche davantage de l'onéreux ou de l'odieux'), which Pufendorf's shorter report lacks.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The custom that successors renew even real alliances is in Pufendorf VIII.9.8 and not in Grotius or Wolff; Vattel takes it over, giving his own reason.

rejudge.label: open disagreement
rejudge.reason: Vattel names Pufendorf (note: Liv. VIII ch. IX § 8) for the rules on successors and treaties, quotes rules 1 and 2, and calls them beside the point.

rejudge.label: open disagreement
rejudge.reason: Vattel names Pufendorf's third rule of VIII.9.8 and declares it as useless to the question as the first two.

rejudge.label: open disagreement
rejudge.reason: Vattel restates Pufendorf's third rule almost word for word and then rejects it as foreign to the question of real and personal treaties.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: Vattel explicitly adopts, 'avec PUFENDORF', the comparison with a man who paid what he did not owe, from VIII.9.8 rule 3.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same point, but Vattel's wording ('ne se présume pas aisément') and his exception for acts admitting no other interpretation follow Grotius II.15.14 and Wolff JG § 433; Pufendorf flatly denies tacit renewal.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Breach releasing the other party is common doctrine; Vattel's choice between compelling and breaking, and the promise as conditional, follow Wolff JG §§ 430, 117 and Grotius II.15.15 rather than Pufendorf.

rejudge.label: open disagreement
rejudge.reason: Vattel names Pufendorf (note: VIII.9.12), quotes his judgment that the Caudine treaty had nothing too harsh, and rejects it.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Rescinding subjects' contract rights by eminent domain is in Grotius II.14.7 as well as Pufendorf VIII.10.7; Vattel's definition of eminent domain follows Wolff (Inst. § 1065).

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel II.214-216 follows Wolff JG § 478 (contract with the nation, 'unde sequitur' it binds nation and successors; same for foreigners and subjects); Pufendorf states the same doctrine in other words.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The clause 'le pouvoir d'obliger le corps de l'état par les dettes qu'il contracte' is nearly verbatim Pufendorf VIII.10.8, with the same limit drawn from the nature of the thing and the same point that the debt binds whatever its success.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same specific argument as Pufendorf VIII.10.9: gifts out of the state's domain must rest on a good reason and can otherwise be taken back; Vattel opens by contrasting donations with debts, answering Pufendorf's 'mêmes principes'.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same sequence as Pufendorf VIII.10.9: privileges and immunities treated like donations and revocable when contrary to the state's good (the 'pure libéralité' phrase comes from Grotius II.14.13).

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Barbeyrac's note mentions Eugene IV voiding Ladislas's treaty with Amurath only in passing; Vattel cites Solignac's Histoire de Pologne, from which his details (Cesarini, Varna, epitaph) come.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Stock doctrine that the oath adds no new obligation; Vattel's wording and the nullity clause follow Wolff (JG § 425, Inst. § 446) as much as Pufendorf IV.2.6.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel II.226 follows Wolff JG § 425 step by step ('Quoniam juramentum non novam producit obligationem...', oath personal, sworn real treaty passes to successors); Pufendorf only states the same doctrine.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: 'Ne change point la nature' echoes Pufendorf IV.2.11 (and its margin), but it is a stock maxim and Vattel's argument here follows Wolff JG § 425 ('juramentum in ipso foedere nil immutat').

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The clause is close to Pufendorf V.12.7, but it is the natural rendering of a stock example that Wolff JG § 553 (the paragraph's frame) and Grotius II.16.5 (whom Vattel cites) also give.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's frame follows Wolff JG § 553, but the Rhadamistus sentence takes Pufendorf V.12.7's French wording ('ni ... fer, ni ... poison, le fit étouffer sous un tas de') and the same order of examples.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The remark that Livy says nothing of the episode matches Pufendorf V.12.7's margin ('ne dit rien de cela'); Barbeyrac's Grotius note, which supplies the name Labeo, says Livy reports it differently.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The definition of tacit consent is stock; 'se déduit, par une juste conséquence' echoes Pufendorf III.6.2, but 'des démarches' and the foi tacite clause follow Wolff (Inst. §§ 27, 271), so the link is not specific.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Antichresis is a stock Roman-law definition; Vattel's sequence (towns and provinces pledged, by deed as hypothec or delivered, revenues for interest) follows Wolff JG §§ 484-485.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Pufendorf reaches the same conclusion, but Vattel's paragraph (liberty pledged, captivity, killing as an error about one's right over one's life) follows Wolff JG §§ 501, 532.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Common doctrine; Vattel's reasoning and sequence (sovereign disposes of subjects so may give them as hostages, indemnity, vassal exception) follow Grotius III.20.52 and Wolff JG §§ 510-514.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Indemnifying the hostage is also in Grotius III.20.52, in the sequence Vattel follows; Pufendorf's 'indemniser ... de la dépense' is a slightly closer wording but not distinctive.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Pufendorf VIII.8.6 has the rule, but Vattel's wording follows Wolff JG § 519 ('alio idoneo substituto', equal security, the treaty did not intend the king as hostage).

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's paragraph follows Wolff JG §519 (release with an equivalent substitute; the treaty never made the king a hostage; the giver would not have consented), and Barbeyrac's note only states the same presumption of the state's non-consent.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's sentence follows Wolff JG §534 (the sovereign may give hostages but has no right to hand an innocent citizen into captivity by breaking faith); Barbeyrac's remark that the state may risk subjects' lives for the public good is the common eminent-domain doctrine.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same specific case as Pufendorf VIII.2.6: the receiving party breaks faith first and the state, to save itself, abandons the hostages; Wolff has no such case (Vattel then departs from Pufendorf by requiring compensation).

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's compensation of hostages 'en leur personne ou en celle de leurs proches' with rewards follows Wolff JG §536 (repensare obsidi aut proximis, praemiis) and Grotius III.20.52; Pufendorf only says the state should refund hostages' losses and costs of absence.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Wolff JG §§538 and 532 (hostage ceases to be one and may be held as captive in perpetual prison); Barbeyrac's note only says they become like prisoners of war, in other words.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's appeal to a generous prince sparing an innocent, and the following options of release on conditions, follow Wolff JG §539 (generosi animi, obsides innocentes); Barbeyrac makes forbearance a duty, not generosity.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Barbeyrac's note gives the same rule against the one who 'pouvoit & devoit' speak clearly and the same two Digest references (D.2.14.39, then D.18.1.21) in the same order that Vattel quotes in his note.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's wording (acceptance 'se rapporte aux paroles' of the offerer, which are taken as repeated in the promise; the acceptor is the true promisor) follows Grotius II.16.32 closely; Pufendorf III.6.15 only states the same doctrine briefly.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same Cicero example of a husband leaving 'tout son argent' to his wife, with the cash-versus-debts question in Barbeyrac's terms ('coffre', 'billets'); the sentence is nearly the same clause, so close paraphrase fits better.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's Mahomet II at Negropont anecdote matches Pufendorf V.12.3 almost word for word and is paired, as only Pufendorf pairs it, with Tamerlan, for which Vattel cites this section.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's anecdote follows Pufendorf's main text (spared head, cut in two); Barbeyrac's note gives a different Cuspinian account (two men promised their lives, the commander of Chalcis), none of which Vattel uses.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Tamerlan at Sebaste, promise not to shed blood, garrison buried alive: nearly verbatim from Pufendorf V.12.3, which Vattel cites in his note.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Pufendorf's sequence (Mahomet, Tamerlan, then 'grossières' quibbles and Cicero on fraud aggravating perjury), but in other words ('échappatoires', 'aggraver la faute'; 'ne font que' echoes Grotius II.16.2).

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: 'Toutes ces misérables subtilités' right after the Tamerlan example echoes Pufendorf's 'Toutes ces subtilitez ... misérables chicanes' at the same point; the rule that follows is Wolff's.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: Vattel's note to the Tamerlan example names Pufendorf V.12.3, where the Tamerlan perfidy is told.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's wording ('la définition qu'en donnent les maîtres de l'art ... l'art ou la science') matches Pufendorf V.12.4 rather than Grotius II.16.3 ('le sens que leur donnent les Maîtres') or Wolff.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's general exception follows Wolff Inst. §802 ('nisi adsint rationes urgentes'), but his specific example, a speaker who does not understand the art, matches Barbeyrac's note ('celui qui parle n'entende ni l'Art').

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's rule and presumption translate Wolff (Inst. §803: 'significatus conveniens materiae, de qua agitur', the sense that could occur to the speaker); Pufendorf states the same stock maxim of the jurists.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's definitions of natural day (while the sun shines) and civil day (twenty-four hours) follow Pufendorf V.12.7, which adds them to Grotius II.16.5 and is cited in Vattel's note.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Cleomenes' truce of some days with Argos and the sleeping Argives on the third night/day are nearly verbatim from Pufendorf V.12.7, called a 'misérable chicane' in both and cited in Vattel's note.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The Antiochus ships sawn in half come from Pufendorf V.12.7, which Vattel cites here; at §233 Vattel uses Pufendorf's wording and his Valerius Maximus/Livy margin, though Grotius II.16.5 also has the example.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: Vattel's note after the Cleomenes example names Pufendorf V.12.7, where that example is told.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: Vattel's note names Pufendorf V.XII.7, so the citation holds (corrected by the editor: the judge rated it wrong because the paired source sentence, on arms in a capitulation, is not the one Vattel's examples follow).

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's rule ('Comme on ne présume point que personne veuille ce qui est absurde', interpret so as to avoid the absurd) translates Wolff Inst. §804 ('nemo absurdum velle praesumitur'); Pufendorf states the same presumption.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: That no one can foresee every case is a commonplace (also Pufendorf V.12.21; Wolff Inst. §810 on circumstances not in mind); Vattel uses it for the absurdity rule, not for Pufendorf's extension of laws.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's limit 'autant qu'il est nécessaire pour éviter' the absurd, after words 'prises dans leur sens propre' lead there, follows Pufendorf V.xii.8; Grotius II.xvi.6 and Wolff Inst. §804 lack this limit.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's sequence (no one is presumed to mean to do nothing, so an interpretation that nullifies the act is not admitted, as a branch of the absurdity rule) follows Wolff Inst. §804; Barbeyrac's note shares the doctrine and 'acte sérieux' but not the sentence structure.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The rule and its derivation from the absurdity rule follow Wolff Inst. §804 ('ea interpretatio non admittenda, qua stante sequitur nihil actum esse'); 'nul & sans effet' is Barbeyrac's stock doublet, also in Grotius II.xvi.10 and Pufendorf V.xii.12.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's 'les Athéniens, après avoir promis de sortir des terres des Béotiens ... les terres qu'occupoit leur armée' matches Pufendorf V.xii.8 (Grotius's text names Brasidas), though 'prétendirent pouvoir rester' echoes Grotius II.xvi.6.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The clause is identical in Pufendorf and Grotius II.xvi.6, but Vattel's full sentence goes on with 'ce dont l'ennemi s'étoit emparé pendant la guerre', which only Grotius has, so the sentence follows Grotius.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's 'on doit donner le même sens à ce qu'il aura dit obscurément ailleurs' after a clear statement 'au sujet d'une certaine chose' reproduces Pufendorf V.xii.9; the 'tant que ... changé de volonté' presumption is shaped on Wolff Inst. §805.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel makes 'la liaison & la suite du discours' a head of interpretation as Pufendorf's §9 and margin do, and takes the Digest maxim from Barbeyrac's note attached to these very words.

rejudge.label: verbatim
rejudge.reason: The 'Incivile est, nisi tota lege perspecta' maxim with the Digest I.3.24 reference is in Barbeyrac's note to Pufendorf V.xii.9 n.1 and not in his Grotius.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's rule and proviso (later clauses agree with earlier ones unless they manifestly change them) follow Wolff Inst. §805; the presumption that a person agrees with himself is a commonplace, also in Grotius II.xvi.7.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's gloss of the reason of the law as 'le motif qui a porté à les faire, la vue' follows Pufendorf V.xii.10's 'les motifs & les vûes qui ont porté le Législateur à faire', and its note's 'moiens ... véritable sens'; Grotius II.xvi.8 lacks the gloss.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same example, but Vattel's wording ('on n'avoit d'autres fortifications que des murailles', 'un certain lieu', 'l'unique ... manifestement d'empêcher que l'on ne fit de ce lieu une place forte') follows Grotius II.xvi.20.4; Pufendorf only repeats it in other words.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The two conditions for extension (the sole reason, taken in its full extent) are Grotius II.xvi.20.3, whose 'unique' reason and 'le cas que l'on veut' Vattel echoes next to Grotius's walls example; Pufendorf V.xii.17 only repeats Grotius.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: The note names Pufendorf V.xii.18, where the Pharos story and the frauds-against-the-law discussion stand.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: Vattel's note names Pufendorf V.xii.18 and the Ammianus XXII.16 reference that Barbeyrac's margin gives for the Pharos story.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's transition (the rule just stated also serves to defeat those who seek to elude the laws) mirrors Pufendorf V.xii.18's opening, whose examples and citation follow; Wolff Inst. §812 states only the doctrine.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The Pharos story is retold almost word for word from Pufendorf V.xii.18, which Vattel cites.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same Corinthian ship sale at five drachmas, taken from Pufendorf V.xii.18, which Vattel cites with Herodotus Book VI.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same Tiberius example from Pufendorf V.xii.18's list (executioner first, strangling after), with Vattel adding Sejanus's daughter from the Tacitus reference in Pufendorf's margin.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: 'PUFEND. ibid.' names Pufendorf V.xii.18 for the Corinthian example, which is there.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: 'PUFEND. ibid.' names Pufendorf V.xii.18, the section on frauds against the law where the Corinthian example stands.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: No aid is due to an ally in an unjust war is common doctrine (Grotius II.xxv.4, II.xvi.16; Wolff JG §656 ff.); Vattel's example shares no wording with Pufendorf VIII.vi.14.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's rule (a case where following the words would be too hard on someone is excepted, since no one binds himself to fail himself) follows Wolff Inst. §815; 'trop dur' is also Grotius II.xvi.27, so Pufendorf only states the same doctrine.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The example of being excused from sending auxiliaries while one needs them 'pour sa propre défense' is worded alike in Grotius II.xvi.27 and Pufendorf V.xii.22; nothing ties Vattel to Pufendorf rather than Grotius.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's sentence translates Wolff Inst. §813 ('si materiae, de qua agitur, parum convenit, ut verba tam late sumantur ... restringenda sunt'); Pufendorf V.xii.19 and Grotius II.xvi.24 only state the same doctrine.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The fief granted 'pour lui & ses descendans mâles', not covering males born of daughters 'quoique mâles', is Pufendorf V.xii.19's example (absent from Grotius), closely paraphrased.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's wording of the question is nearly verbatim Grotius II.16.25 (Barbeyrac: 'renferment par elles-mêmes cette condition tacite, Que les choses demeurent dans l'état où elles sont'; cf. Wolff Inst. §814 'in se'), while Pufendorf's version ('& les Engagemens', 'supposé que', 'en l'état') is further off.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel frames the rule positively from the reason of the promise as Wolff Inst. §814 does ('status rerum praesens in ratione sufficiente promissionis'); Pufendorf, like Grotius II.16.25, only states the same doctrine, with no distinctive wording tying Vattel to him.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same example of help promised to an ally lapsing while the promisor needs his forces for his own defence; identical in Grotius II.16.27, but Vattel's 'ses propres états' echoes Pufendorf's next sentence ('la conservation de ses propres Etats').

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's warning that, if any change dissolved promises, none could be relied on reproduces the argument of Barbeyrac's note 2 to Pufendorf (absent from Grotius), but in other words.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The Titus/Galba example is Pufendorf's (not in Grotius II.16.25), used at the same point, but Vattel retells it in his own words with added detail from Tacitus.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's formula ('comme il l'interpréteroit lui-même s'il étoit présent ... s'il eut prévû les choses que l'on connoît présentement') follows Wolff Inst. §810 ('si praesens esset, vel si eidem cognita fuissent, quae nunc palam sunt'); Pufendorf only states the same Aristotelian equity doctrine.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's 'considérées, non comme actuellement existantes' is Grotius II.16.25 verbatim, and his 'only where the event is shown impossible' follows Wolff Inst. §813; Pufendorf's 'existence actuelle ... possibilité Morale' is further off.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same treaty example, but Vattel's wording ('on ne menera point d'armée ou de flotte', 'sans dessein de nuire', 'prévenir ... tout danger') follows Grotius II.16.25, not Pufendorf's ('n'envoiera point', 'ombrage', 'invasion actuelle').

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The torch-at-night law and the excuse of having carried it 'avec tant de circonspection' come from Pufendorf (not in Grotius), in the same sentence shape.

rejudge.label: open disagreement
rejudge.reason: Vattel's complaint is about the received definitions of Grotius and Pufendorf in general, not this clause, which he himself adopts almost unchanged in §301, so no rejection of this passage is shown.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: Vattel's note names Barbeyrac's remarks on Pufendorf for those who reject the distinction, and this note is where Barbeyrac rejects the definitions of the favourable and the odious.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The criteria of common utility and equality are Grotius II.16.10's and Wolff's (JG §420, Inst. §808: 'in pactis ad communem utilitatem spectant & utrique parti aequaliter consulunt'), which Vattel's 'utilité commune dans les conventions' follows; Pufendorf (who has 'Utilité Publique') only restates them, in a different sentence structure.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same criterion in Grotius II.16.10 and Pufendorf, but Vattel's 'charge seulement l'une des parties, ou ce qui la charge plus que l'autre', paired with common utility and equality, follows Wolff JG §420 ('partem alteram tantum onerant, aut plus onerant alteram').

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's 'contribuent au bien de la paix ... menent à la guerre' is Grotius II.16.10's wording ('contribuë au bien de la Paix ... méne à la Guerre'); Pufendorf has 'contribuent à la Paix ... tendent à la Guerre'.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Penalty as odious is a stock maxim found identically in Grotius II.16.10. Vattel's 'contient une peine' and his argument that penal clauses burden one party follow Wolff Inst. §809 ('verba quae poenam continent', 'poena ... onus').

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same pair of odious things (making an act null; changing what was already settled) in nearly the same words; Grotius II.16.10 is equally close, but nothing points away from Pufendorf.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's separate rule against changing the present state of things, grounded on the presumption for the possessor, is his own extension; Pufendorf's item on changes to settled matters is what Vattel already used in §304.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Quintilian's rule that avoiding a loss is the better cause is in Pufendorf but not Grotius, and Vattel's §301 note gives the same reference as Barbeyrac's note (Inst. Orat. VII.4).

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same third class of things partaking of both the favourable and the odious; Grotius II.16.10 has the same classification, so Pufendorf is one of two equally close sources.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same mixed case of a change to an act made for the good of peace, worded the same in Grotius II.16.10 and Pufendorf.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel takes up Barbeyrac's objection in this note, found only in his Pufendorf (that penalties are odious yet serve public utility), and turns it into the mixed status of penalties.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same first rule for favourable matters, giving terms their full extent; Grotius II.16.12 states it in the same words ('on doit donner aux termes'), and in §307 Vattel is using Pufendorf §13 (Caecina, Digest).

rejudge.label: verbatim
rejudge.reason: Same words as Barbeyrac's Pufendorf, which are also identical in his Grotius II.16.12.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's 'arrêt interlocutoire', 'héritage' and the following 'c'est tout un' come from Pufendorf §13 rather than Grotius ('Fonds'), though 'soutient avec raison' echoes Grotius.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's Digest reference (De vi et vi armata, Leg. I & III) matches Barbeyrac's note 4 to Pufendorf (Leg. III §8, Leg. I §24) for the same Caecina point.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Pufendorf's own gloss on Cicero's pro Caecina case ('c'est tout un ... de l'empêcher d'y rentrer'), absent from Grotius II.16.12, reappears in Vattel together with the Digest laws Pufendorf/Barbeyrac cite.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same second rule on favourable matters in the same structure, generalised from jurisprudence to any art; Pufendorf's 'En matiére de' and 's'il se conduit' are closer than Grotius II.16.12.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same fourth rule (restrict the proper sense to avoid absurdity or injustice), with Pufendorf's order 'absurdité, ou quelque injustice' rather than Grotius's.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same fifth rule with the clause 'on doit s'en tenir au sens le plus étroit que la signification propre (des termes) souffre'; Vattel's 'équité manifeste' is Grotius's wording, which Barbeyrac's note 9 here restores.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same rule on odious matters in nearly the same words (admit the figurative sense to avoid the onerous consequences of the literal one); Grotius II.16.12 has the identical rule.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Both concern aid troops furnished 'à ses propres dépens', but Vattel's explicit-clause case only applies his clear-terms rule to the Grotius/Pufendorf example; nothing ties it specifically to Barbeyrac's note, and it is not the same content.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same example: aid promised without mention of cost is understood at the expense of the receiving party; Grotius II.16.12 gives it in near-identical words.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel names Grotius and quotes Grotius II.16.13 verbatim; Pufendorf VIII.9.10 only restates the same question in other words.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's sentence reproduces Pufendorf's own summary of Grotius's decision ('sans préjudice du Traité, les Carthaginois pouvoient attaquer Sagonte'), almost word for word.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Both mention the Roman quibble over the meaning of 'Carthage', but Vattel names Grotius (II.16.15) and uses his word 'chicane'; Pufendorf only reports the same point.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same argument that the promised liberty, though limited, must at least leave the Carthaginians their city, in Pufendorf's wording ('la liberté promise aux Carthaginois ... devoit'), with his razing-and-sea details nearby, though Vattel credits Grotius.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same definition of conflict: two laws or conventions, not contradictory and performable at different times, that cannot be satisfied at once; the 'different times' clause is Pufendorf's, not Grotius's.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same first rule with Pufendorf's specific reason (simple permission leaves liberty to act or not, a command removes it); Grotius and Wolff give other reasons.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The clause 'si l'on ne peut obéir à une loi affirmative sans violer une loi négative' is word for word Pufendorf's, with only the next verb changed.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same reason, in the same contrast: negative law binds absolutely, affirmative law presupposes a favourable occasion, which then is lacking.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same next step of Pufendorf's argument, that the conflict makes observance morally impossible (Wolff Inst. § 64 has the same phrase, but the sequence is Pufendorf's).

rejudge.label: verbatim
rejudge.reason: Identical clause; Vattel's opening 'De deux loix, ou de deux conventions' and his named use of Pufendorf's example show he follows Pufendorf here (Grotius II.16.29 has the same clause).

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: Vattel names Pufendorf and gives his festival-day arms and tocsin example in nearly his words.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same rule that what must be done now prevails over what can be done at any time, with the reason Pufendorf's gloss gives (defer the other so both are satisfied).

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same rule framed as Pufendorf frames it (conflict of two duties, the 'plus considérable' with greater honesty or utility prevails), unlike Grotius's bare rule.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Pufendorf's separate rule for laws (nobler, more useful, more necessary) matches, and Vattel's Cicero note reproduces the 'Primum igitur leges...' quotation from Barbeyrac's note on this §.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: The note cites Pufendorf V.12.23 correctly for the tocsin example, though the paired excerpt is a different sentence of that §.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same oath rule, but Vattel's wording ('conflict', 'le premier l'emporte') is closer to Grotius II.16.29 and his limit follows Wolff JG § 427; Pufendorf's sentence only states the same rule.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The penalty rule is Grotius's (II.16.29), and Vattel adopts it with the reason in Barbeyrac's note to Grotius; Pufendorf only reports it in the same words in order to doubt it.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same specific counsel Pufendorf adds to Grotius: an intermediary, unlike an arbiter bound to strict justice, should urge a party to give up part of its right.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's point that submitting only to a sentence one finds just would make arbitration useless restates Pufendorf V.13.4's argument against a submission 'supposé que la sentence fût juste'; Wolff's Jus gentium has no such argument.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same specific exception as Pufendorf V.13.4: an award binds unless it manifestly comes from collusion, bribery or open partiality of the arbiter (Barbeyrac's Grotius note points to this very §).

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Favouring the possessor until the claimant proves his right is a stock maxim; Vattel's wording (show the possession unjust, no arms for a doubtful right) is closer to Grotius II.23.11.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Trying peaceful means before taking arms is a commonplace; Vattel refers back to his § 334 (Wolff § 630, Grotius II.23.11), and Barbeyrac's note only states the same maxim.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Stock definition of talion; Vattel's 'autant de mal qu'il en a fait' is closer to Grotius I.2.5 ('souffre autant de mal qu'il en a fait') and Wolff Inst. § 156 than to Pufendorf's 'le même mal'.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The ancient name 'droit de Rhadamanthe' (from Aristotle) is a shared tag, also in Grotius I.2.5 and II.20.1; nothing ties Vattel to Barbeyrac's note in particular.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Requiring a clear cause for reprisals is shared doctrine (Grotius III.2.5, Wolff, Burlamaqui); Vattel's sentence on doubtful claims only being entitled to examination is not in Barbeyrac's note.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Subjects' goods answering for the state's debts is common doctrine (Grotius III.2.2); Vattel cites his own §§ 18 and 82, which follow Wolff JG §§ 289 and 495.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Wolff JG § 601 (loss repaid from public funds, each bearing his share pro rata = 'quote-part'); Pufendorf VIII.6.13 only states the same doctrine, in a different sentence.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Sovereign-only reprisals is shared doctrine; Vattel's 'donc' follows Wolff JG §§ 589-590, and the near-war reason he adds also appears in Barbeyrac's note on Grotius III.2.7.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Wolff JG §§ 591-593 on androlepsia (citizens held as pledges until justice is done); Barbeyrac's note only states the same rule.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's wording and reason follow Wolff JG § 595 ('nec poena corporis afflictiva'; no one owns his life, but liberty can be pledged); Barbeyrac's note only states the ban on killing them.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: That private persons lose the right of war in civil society is common doctrine (Grotius, Wolff, Burlamaqui); Vattel grounds it in his own II.49ff., not in Pufendorf's wording.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same specific argument and wording: a king who cannot raise money or compel subjects to arms without another body has a war right that 'se réduit' to little (Pufendorf VII.4.12).

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The objects of offensive war (claim, punish, prevent) follow Wolff JG §§ 615-619; Pufendorf VIII.6.3 only gives the same common classification.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same anecdote of the bishop who killed enemies with a mace to avoid shedding blood; in the corpus only Barbeyrac's note has it, with the details Vattel uses.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's note gives the same identifying details, in the same order, as Barbeyrac's note: bishop of Beauvais, under Philip Augustus, at Bouvines.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The presumption of the powers an office needs is a stock maxim; Vattel's paragraph follows Wolff JG § 771, and Grotius III.22.4 ('présomtion... bien exercer les fonctions') is as close.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's numbered triple end is a translation of Wolff JG § 619 (same order, 'duo priores offensivo, tertius defensivo'); Pufendorf VIII.6.3 states the doctrine in another order and wording.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Wolff JG § 629 ('injustum est defensivum si offensivum fuerit justum'); Barbeyrac's quoted note makes the same point in a different sentence.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's reason for declaring war (a last chance for the enemy to do justice before arms) follows Wolff JG § 710; Barbeyrac's note gives the same rationale only in general terms.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Wolff JG § 713 (defensive war need not be declared); Barbeyrac's note holds the same doctrine against Grotius but with a different reason.

rejudge.label: verbatim
rejudge.reason: Vattel names and quotes Grotius I.3.4 verbatim; Pufendorf VIII.6.9 only repeats the same Grotian formula, so nothing points to Pufendorf.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same caution not to stretch a tacit restriction or allies will find pretexts to evade the treaty, but Pufendorf's restriction concerns separate peace, not the just-war clause Vattel takes from Wolff § 659.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's absurdity argument is Wolff JG § 669; Barbeyrac's note (after Grotius) holds the just ally must be helped even against another ally, which Vattel's sentence denies.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Barbeyrac's neutrality note gives Vattel's two-part rule (no war supplies to either side unless bound by engagement; equal treatment in non-war things), with the echo 'fournir ... ce qui sert à la guerre'; Wolff §683 has the rule but not this wording.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Both say an established custom among nations should be followed, but this is commonplace; Barbeyrac makes it only an imperfect duty, and Vattel's doctrine of custom follows Wolff (Proleg. §24).

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The bare impartiality rule (do not refuse to one what you grant the other) is also in Wolff §§683-684, which Vattel's §118 follows closely (access, buying provisions and horses, neutrality treaties); Barbeyrac's note only states the same doctrine.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Asking passage before forcing it is Grotius II.ii.13.4, whom Vattel follows with the same Agesilaus-returning-from-Asia example; Wolff §§687-688 has asking and paying; Pufendorf only states the same doctrine.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Seizing a neutral place is Grotius's doctrine (II.ii.10), which Pufendorf only reports; Vattel's wording (extreme necessity, return when danger is past, paying damages) is closest to Barbeyrac's neutrality note at VIII.vi.7 n.2, not this passage.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Against Grotius and Wolff §686, Vattel takes Pufendorf's argument that receiving a large foreign force at home is itself a danger justifying refusal ('recevoir chez soi', the experience of nations).

rejudge.label: open disagreement
rejudge.reason: Vattel rejects Grotius's claim, citing Grotius II.ii.13 directly ('crainte injuste' echoes Wolff §686), while Pufendorf reports that claim only to argue against it; Vattel sides with Pufendorf, so there is no disagreement with this source.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Grant or refuse passage to both sides, on pain of not keeping 'exacte neutralité', follows Wolff §§684-685 (neutralitate non exacte servata); the only parallel with Barbeyrac's general rule is an 'unless a reason' clause whose sense differs.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The argument (the other belligerent asks passage too, the armies meet, the country becomes the theatre of war with endless harm, and one may join the other side against the one who forces it) follows Wolff §696 more fully; Pufendorf has only the theatre-of-war point.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: They share only the stock example of Caesar refusing the Helvetians (also in Grotius's own note to II.ii.13), used for different points: Pufendorf for fear of disorder, Vattel for an unjust war.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's booty passage follows Wolff §§852-855 (booty is the sovereign's, soldiers are his instruments, auxiliaries have no right, he disposes of it as he pleases); Pufendorf only states the same doctrine.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The impossibility of fixing the necessary extent of hostilities, no judge among nations, each belligerent judging, and endless disputes all follow Wolff §783; Pufendorf VIII.vi.15 states the same point with only a phrasal echo.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's case for keeping faith in wartime conventions uses Barbeyrac's specific argument that they limit the fury of arms, which would otherwise have no bounds ('fureur', 'bornes'), in the same anti-Pufendorf context; the 'common interest of both' part is from Wolff §799.

rejudge.label: open disagreement
rejudge.reason: Vattel's tacit-waiver argument ('otherwise nothing would be done, absurd to treat') is Wolff §799 almost word for word; it contradicts Pufendorf's denial only implicitly, without taking it up.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Release when the enemy breaks a convention first is stock doctrine (Grotius III.xix, Wolff on foedera, Vattel's own II §202), mentioned only in passing in Barbeyrac's note; the sentences do not share structure.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Besides Wolff's term falsiloquium, Vattel takes from Barbeyrac's note on lying the clause 'n'ont aucun droit d'exiger qu'on leur dise' and the framing against theologians who forbid every false speech.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: That the licence to deceive an enemy does not reach conventions is common doctrine (Grotius, Wolff §857); Vattel's reason ('absurd ... ce seroit ne rien faire') is Wolff §799's, not Pufendorf's reason from the duty of peace.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Both hold that suborning enemy subjects is permitted as against the enemy, but Vattel's reason (it does not threaten the common safety of mankind) is his own, and he then condemns the practice as dishonest, against Pufendorf.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's reply to Grotius uses the argument from Pufendorf and Barbeyrac's note: subjects cannot weigh the justice of every order without making government impossible.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same note: a presumption that superiors' orders are just until there is manifest or absolute evidence to the contrary, in the same sentence structure ('présumer ... tant que ... du contraire').

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's sentence (expletio juris, retaining as equivalent of what is due, expenses and penalty) follows Wolff §859; Pufendorf states the same just-war acquisition doctrine.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's measure (what is due or its equivalent, war costs, and retaining places for security against a dangerous enemy, weakening him) follows Pufendorf VIII.vi.17's sequence, which adds security and weakening to Grotius III.xiii and Wolff.

rejudge.label: open disagreement
rejudge.reason: Vattel answers Pufendorf's rule that a people freed by a third party merely changes master with his own words ('non pour lui faire changer seulement de maître'); his duty in conscience to free the people comes from Grotius III.xvi.4.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Grounding postliminium in the sovereign's duty to defend subjects is in Pufendorf VIII.vi.22 but also in Wolff §§903 and 1020, and the rest of Vattel's §205 follows Wolff §§894-895.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: 'Rétablir ... dans tous leurs droits & dans toutes leurs obligations' renders Wolff §894 ('omnibus eorum juribus ipsis & aliorum juribus in ipsos restitutis'); Pufendorf's 'premier état ... tous leurs droits' states the same doctrine.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's §213 follows Pufendorf VIII.vi.23's sequence (people freed by own forces or an ally regains 'sans contredit' its 'ancien état'; a non-allied liberator), though it reverses Pufendorf on the non-ally; Grotius III.ix.9 has only the ally case.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The sovereign granting all or part of the booty is common doctrine; Vattel's privateer passage follows Grotius III.xviii.2-3 (with Barbeyrac's note), and Pufendorf's passage concerns soldiers' pillage in general.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's 'ne differe guere de la paix, sinon en ce qu'elle laisse indécise la question' follows Wolff JG §890; Pufendorf only says a long truce resembles peace.

rejudge.locus: Liv. VIII ch. VII § 2, n. §. VIII. 1
rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Barbeyrac's note only restates Grotius III.xxi.5; Vattel's sequence (binds parties at once, subjects only on notice, unknown law cannot oblige, restitution) follows Wolff JG §919 and Grotius.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Pufendorf copies Grotius III.xxi.11 almost word for word, and Wolff §935 has the same rule; nothing ties Vattel's sentence to Pufendorf in particular.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same rule as Grotius III.xxi.12 (with Barbeyrac's note on damages) and Wolff §935 ('la peine payée, les trêves subsistent'), which Vattel's wording follows; the Pufendorf sentence is phrased differently.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Pufendorf's reason (the fine is paid so the accord stays whole) is Grotius III.xxi.12's; Vattel's sentence belongs to his argument on the alternative clause, which follows Wolff §936.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: On the disputed question ('les auteurs se partagent') Vattel takes Pufendorf's side against Grotius that the first day is included, with the same ordinary-meaning argument.

rejudge.label: open disagreement
rejudge.reason: Vattel's ban on bringing in relief follows Grotius III.xxi.10 and Wolff §928 ('tout doit demeurer dans l'état'); he neither names nor answers Pufendorf here, and §249 then grants Pufendorf's point for limited truces.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The distinction of a special-purpose truce, with the burial example, is already in Grotius III.xxi.10 (and Wolff §932); this sentence alone does not single out Pufendorf, whose conclusion Vattel adopts only in the next sentences.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel adopts Pufendorf's position against Grotius, Wolff and Barbeyrac that the besieged may bring in relief during such a truce, in the same construction ('rien n'empêche que ... ne fasse entrer').

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Pufendorf's specific claim, rejected by Grotius and Barbeyrac, that during a burial truce one may retire to a safer post without breaking one's word, in matching wording.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Pufendorf's argument that the party who granted the limited truce must blame only himself ('ne doit s'en prendre qu'à lui-même') reappears as 'ne pourra s'en prendre qu'à sa propre négligence'.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The rule is Grotius III.xxi.9, which Pufendorf only cites; Vattel's reason ('accident qu'ils pouvoient prévoir') follows Wolff JG §929 and his appeal to humanity follows Grotius.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The rule itself is stock (Grotius III.xxi.3, Wolff §916), but Vattel's §260 follows Pufendorf VIII.vii.6's sequence: no new declaration, then a declaration that is fitting after a long truce that 'fait disparoître tout l'appareil'.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: 'Ressemble fort à la paix' is Pufendorf's phrase for the long truce, and it sits in a paragraph that follows Pufendorf VIII.vii.6; Wolff §890 has a different formula.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: 'Laisse subsister le sujet de la guerre' repeats Pufendorf's marginal summary to VIII.vii.5 word for word, in a paragraph that follows Pufendorf's truce chapter.

rejudge.label: citation
rejudge.reason: Vattel's note names Pufendorf VIII.vii.14 for the Procopius story, which he gives in Pufendorf's words.

rejudge.locus: Liv. VIII ch. VII § 2, n. §. XII. 1
rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's clause matches the note's wording closely ('lui appartiennent, en sorte qu'il puisse s'en servir pour le paiement de sa rançon'), although the doctrine is Grotius III.xxi.28's and is also in Wolff §§956-957.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: A stock definition; Vattel's wording ('On appelle rebelles', to strip him of power or impose conditions) follows Wolff JG §1010 / Inst. §1232, not the note.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Pufendorf only states the doctrine; Vattel's amnesty point and his argument follow Wolff JG §§1015-1016 and Grotius III.xix.7.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Pufendorf's note 4 types civil war as two opposed parties in republics and, in a monarchy, two pretenders, and Vattel's §292 reproduces this typology (the wording 'prétendans à la couronne' is also in Grotius II.xviii.2).

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same definition in nearly the same words ('membres d'une même société'), in a paragraph that also uses note 4 attached to this sentence.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The definition of rebellion is stock (also Wolff JG §1010, already used in Vattel §288), and Vattel's criterion 'destitué de toute apparence de justice' is his own.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: A Cicero commonplace (De off. I.11), which Vattel quotes directly in his note; Grotius II.xxiii.7 also has it.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The 'otherwise no one could treat safely' argument is generic (cf. Grotius III.20.10); Pufendorf applies it to ceding private goods, while Vattel's paragraph on tacit consent follows Wolff JG §1007.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Stock doctrine from Grotius III.20.7 that Pufendorf repeats; Vattel's sequence (goods by eminent domain, persons by eminent power) follows Wolff JG §1008.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Compensation from public funds is Grotius III.20.7.3, which Pufendorf copies; Vattel refers to his own I.244, so nothing points to Pufendorf.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Wolff JG §984 (other nations must stand by the nation's judgment and follow possession, yet may aid the dispossessed king); Pufendorf states only the general non-interference point.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's paragraph (perpetual peace means not for the same cause; special versus general transaction) follows Wolff JG §987; Pufendorf only states the same doctrine.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The auxiliary-troops exception is Grotius II.16.27, which Pufendorf copies almost word for word, and Wolff JG §665 has the same rule, so nothing singles out Pufendorf.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's peace-treaty rule ('celui qui a donné la loi', 'il pouvoit s'expliquer plus clairement') follows Grotius III.20.26; Barbeyrac's note gives only the general contract rule.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Grotius III.20.28 ('contre ... tout traité de paix', plausible pretext) and Wolff JG §1021 (same cause or wartime acts); Pufendorf only states the doctrine.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same justification in the same context: a new cause does not break the peace because peace is no engagement to suffer every injury without resisting; neither Wolff §1025 nor Grotius gives it.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's 'comme nous venons de le voir' points to his quotation of Grotius III.19.14 in IV.47 ('en forme de condition'); Pufendorf calls it the common maxim.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same rule and alternatives: an offender caught in a masterless place or on the open sea may be dealt with directly, or, if one prefers, one may complain to his sovereign.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's chain (necessity and right of embassies, so their security and persons are sacred by the common safety of nations) follows Wolff JG §1065; Barbeyrac's note states the same doctrine.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same syllogism as Barbeyrac's (Buddeus) note: natural law requires intercourse among nations, 'or' ambassadors are necessary to it, so they are protected by natural law, not convention (here against Wolff §1059).

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Like Barbeyrac's note, and going beyond Grotius II.18.4 (who allows killing only against armed force), Vattel allows arresting and even killing an envoy when necessary for safety; the wording is recast.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Grotius II.18.7 (cited in his note; 'maltraiter un Ambassadeur par droit de représailles', Scipio); Barbeyrac's note only states the rule.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same rebuttal of the claim that a prince entering incognito may be arrested ('en vertu dequoi ... cette violence'), and Vattel's note cites the same Gramond passage as Pufendorf's margin.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Part of the same Pufendorf argument: after rejecting arrest, both concede that the prince should not come unannounced or without leave.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same doctrine, against Bynkershoek ch. XI: a former subject accredited as a foreign minister is exempt from his old state's jurisdiction, followed by the same corollary.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same corollary in the same sentence form: if the state will not grant him this independence or honour, it may refuse to receive him as minister.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: 'Personne morale' with its own will, rights and duties is stock (Pufendorf); Vattel's 'capable d'obligations & de droits' matches Wolff's Praefatio ('personae morales ... subjecta jurium & obligationum').

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's 'n'est originairement ... que le droit de la nature appliqué aux nations' is Wolff JG Prol. §3 ('originarie ... Jus naturae ad Gentes applicatum'); Burlamaqui gives the Hobbesian formula.

rejudge.label: open disagreement
rejudge.reason: Vattel's preface names Hobbes and Pufendorf II.3.23 as targets, and Burlamaqui copies that sentence verbatim; Vattel's correction follows Wolff's Praefatio.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's inference (necessary law is natural law applied, natural law is immutable, so necessary law is immutable) is Wolff JG Prol. §5; Burlamaqui only states it in passing.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's rule that treaties or customs contrary to necessary law are illegitimate follows Wolff's Prolegomena (§6); Burlamaqui's point that usages may be unjust is a different, general remark.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Priority of duties to oneself is Wolff JG §206 ('officium gentis erga seipsam vincit'); Burlamaqui's ranked rule, qualified 'toutes choses égales', is common stock.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's definition translates Wolff's Institutiones § 80 (jus cogendi alterum si obligationi satisfacere nolit); Burlamaqui gives the stock coercion-based definition in different words.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Only the terms match: Burlamaqui's internal/external obligation is reason versus a superior's command, while Vattel's is conscience versus obligation towards others producing rights, in Wolff's sense.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel recalls his own Prelim. § 6, which translates Wolff's Jus gentium § 3 ('non est nisi jus naturae ad gentes applicatum'); Burlamaqui states the same common definition.

rejudge.locus: Part. II ch. VI § VIII, n. 4
rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's frame follows Wolff's Jus gentium § 707 and points back to his own Prelim. § 26; the 'binding until renounced' clause is also in Barbeyrac's note on Pufendorf II.3.23, and nothing here is specific to Burlamaqui.

rejudge.locus: Part. II ch. XI (imputation, cause principale)
rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui applies the principal-cause rule specifically to subjects serving in an unjust war as mere instruments, the sovereign alone being responsible, which is the position Vattel takes against Grotius.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel repeats Burlamaqui's own reworking of Barbeyrac: a custom innocent (indifferent) in itself, once introduced, binds a nation until it declares it will no longer conform.

rejudge.locus: Partie II, ch. VI, §. IX, note 1
rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui's note copies Barbeyrac's note 3 on Pufendorf II.3.23 (Latin authors use the two terms indifferently, with the Cicero line), the section Vattel's preface quotes verbatim for Hobbes.

rejudge.locus: Partie II, ch. VI, §. IX, note 1
rejudge.label: verbatim
rejudge.reason: The same truncated Cicero quotation (De officiis III.5) stands in Barbeyrac's note on Pufendorf II.3.23, Burlamaqui's own source; a shared ancient proof-text.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's wording ('selon lui', 'ajoute-t-il', 'Les maximes...') is verbatim Pufendorf II.3.23; Burlamaqui only restates the same Hobbes division.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
