rejudge.reason: 'Personne morale' is stock; Vattel's moral person with its own understanding and will follows Wolff's Jus gentium §§ 2, 56-57.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's inference (nations are free persons, so natural law must be applied to them) follows Wolff's Jus gentium §§ 2-3, which his next clause translates; Burlamaqui's phrasing is the same commonplace.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's § 7 translates Wolff's Jus gentium § 4, and the reason that states are made of men still bound by natural law echoes Wolff; 'composés d'hommes' is a commonplace.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The limit that a duty to another nation ceases when it would harm oneself follows Wolff's Jus gentium §§ 156, 206 (duty to self prevails in a collision); Burlamaqui states the stock condition on imperfect duties.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The natural liberty and independence of nations is a stock premise, here from Wolff (Jus gentium § 2; Inst. § 1089) and Vattel's own Prelim. §§ 4-5.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The union of distinct states under one king is Pufendorf VII.5.17 (and Grotius I.3.7), which Burlamaqui repeats; Vattel adds his own Neuchatel example.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui's sentence copies Pufendorf VII.5.18 ('n'exercer que d'un commun consentement certaines parties de la Souveraineté'); Vattel's paragraph opens from Grotius I.3.7.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Fundamental laws as those fixing the form of government and the manner of governing is a common definition; Vattel drops Burlamaqui's contractual frame and nothing specific ties them.

rejudge.label: verbatim
rejudge.reason: 'Opposer la force à la violence' is a stock phrase of the resistance debate; Vattel's paragraph follows Grotius I.4 and Barbeyrac's notes.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The rhetorical question comes from Barbeyrac's note 4 on Grotius II.7.27 ('Or qui peut mieux juger de cela que le Peuple même?'), which Burlamaqui copies and which Vattel is answering there.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Barbeyrac's same note on Grotius II.7.27 already has the people, back in interim independence, decide by itself 'ou ceux qui le représentent'; Burlamaqui restates it.

rejudge.label: verbatim
rejudge.reason: The phrase is Pufendorf VII.7.12 ('nez d'un Mariage conforme aux Loix du Païs'), which Burlamaqui copies; Vattel's clause is as close to Pufendorf.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: That conquest without the conquered's consent leaves the state of war in being is Barbeyrac's note on Grotius (and Locke), which Burlamaqui copies; nothing points to Burlamaqui.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: That power is entrusted to the prince only for the public good is a commonplace; Vattel applies his own § 39 to the power of naming a successor, and the shared words are generic.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui's sentence copies Pufendorf VII.9.11 ('il ne doit rien négliger, pour procurer l'entretien & l'augmentation des biens'), so the frame Vattel shares is Pufendorf's.

rejudge.locus: Part. I ch. III (Du droit du Souverain en matière de religion) § VI
rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same argument against clerical independence in nearly the same words ('établir deux puissances indépendantes dans une même société'), not found in Pufendorf or Grotius.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Pardon as a sovereign right exercised for public utility is stock doctrine, and Burlamaqui's sentence is Barbeyrac's note to Pufendorf VII.4.4 word for word; nothing ties Vattel to Burlamaqui.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui's presumed stipulation for citizens' children is Pufendorf VII.2.20 (Barbeyrac) verbatim, and Vattel's wording follows neither closely, so the shared doctrine cannot be traced to Burlamaqui.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui's sentence is Pufendorf VIII.5.7 (Barbeyrac) verbatim, 'en même tems' included, and Vattel's claim that eminent domain is part of the empire follows Wolff (JG § 104); Burlamaqui only repeats the doctrine.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Abandoning a part of the state in extreme necessity, though it may not be alienated, comes from Barbeyrac's note 1 to Grotius II.6.6, which Burlamaqui paraphrases; the sentences differ in structure.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The abandoned part's right to defend itself 'si elle peut' is Barbeyrac's note to Grotius II.6.6, which Burlamaqui copies; Vattel words it differently, so the source cannot be told.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same claim as Barbeyrac's note to Grotius II.6.6, and Vattel's 'le nouveau maître qu'on voudroit lui donner' is closer to Barbeyrac ('auquel on veut la donner') than to Burlamaqui.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Only the generic consent of 'the people or its representatives' is shared (Grotius III.20.5 has the rule); Vattel makes it conditional on the fundamental law and lets an absolute prince cede, unlike Burlamaqui's flat rule.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The ends of punishment (deter the offender, intimidate others) are commonplace, and Burlamaqui's sentence is Barbeyrac's Locke quotation in the note to Pufendorf VIII.3, so nothing is specific to Burlamaqui.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's non-intervention sentence translates Wolff JG § 256 ('nullus Rector civitatis habet jus regimini alieno se immiscendi'); Burlamaqui only states the common principle, in the context of punitive war.

rejudge.locus: Burlamaqui, Principes du droit politique, Pt. II ch. ? § 47
rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The doctrine that foreigners may aid subjects only when tyranny justifies their own resistance is Pufendorf VIII.6.14 (Barbeyrac), which Burlamaqui copies verbatim; Vattel shares it with that common source.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's brief sentence (demand justice of the culprit's sovereign) matches only the stock punish-or-deliver rule of Grotius II.21.4, which Burlamaqui copies from Barbeyrac; no wording is paraphrased.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Tolls that compensate road upkeep are in Pufendorf III.3.7 (Barbeyrac: 'on se dédommage ... des frais ... entretenir les chemins'), which Vattel's wording matches as well as Burlamaqui's.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel names Grotius II.15.5 here and copies Barbeyrac's wording exactly ('tenu', where Burlamaqui has 'obligé'), so the source is Grotius and Burlamaqui is a parallel copy.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The ancients' need for such treaties comes from Grotius II.15.5 (cited by Vattel) and Pufendorf VIII.9.2, which Burlamaqui paraphrases; Vattel's 'not among their allies' is closer to Grotius and Pufendorf than to Burlamaqui's 'Concitoyens'.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's point that treaties of non-injury are useful among nations who think they may harm foreigners follows Wolff JG § 392; Burlamaqui only repeats Pufendorf VIII.9.2 on the ancients.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's argument (non-injury treaties not necessary but useful, since contracted obligation binds more firmly) follows Wolff JG § 392-393; Burlamaqui's 'ne sont pas nécessaires' paraphrases Pufendorf VIII.9.2.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's definition follows Wolff JG § 395 ('eadem aut aequivalentia'), and Burlamaqui's is Pufendorf VIII.9.3 almost word for word; the proportion clause is common to that stock.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The division by the side of the inequality, with 'du côté de la Puissance la plus considérable', is Barbeyrac's Grotius II.15.7.2 verbatim, which Burlamaqui copies; Wolff JG § 398 has the same division.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's definition of unequal treaties renders Wolff JG § 398 ('eadem aut aequivalentia non promittuntur'); Burlamaqui only repeats Pufendorf VIII.9.4.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The division into personal and real treaties is stock (Grotius II.16.16, Pufendorf VIII.9.6, Wolff JG § 412).

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui copies Barbeyrac's Grotius II.16.16.2 ('changé de Républicain en Monarchique ... ne laisse pas de subsister'), which Vattel follows along with Wolff JG § 416; nothing points to Burlamaqui.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The exception for two republics allied to keep their liberty is Grotius II.16.16.2 and Pufendorf VIII.9.6; Burlamaqui only repeats it.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui's presumption is Barbeyrac's note 6 to Grotius II.16.16 (after Thomasius) verbatim, and Vattel, following Wolff JG § 423-424, states it only 'd'abord' and then qualifies it.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's rule matches Wolff JG § 417 ('in perpetuum, aut ad certum tempus ... reale est') and Grotius II.16.16.4 ('certain tems limité') more closely than Burlamaqui's 'certain nombre d'années'.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: 'Pour lui & ses Successeurs ... on voit assez par là que le Traité est réel' is Barbeyrac's Grotius II.16.16.4 verbatim, which Burlamaqui copies; Vattel follows that common source.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui copies Grotius II.15.14 (Barbeyrac): 'car une nouvelle obligation ne se présume pas aisément'; Vattel's phrase can come from Grotius as well, and his rule follows Wolff JG § 433.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's 'actes ... qui ne peuvent être faits qu'en vertu du traité' renders Wolff JG § 433 ('quod nonnisi vi ejusdem fieri poterat'); Burlamaqui only repeats Grotius II.15.14's exception, in a different sentence.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The annual-payment example is Barbeyrac's note 2 to Grotius II.15.14, which Burlamaqui copies verbatim; Vattel, who uses Barbeyrac's Grotius in the next §§, reworks it (continued, not renewed), so nothing points to Burlamaqui.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's choice between compelling the ally and breaking the treaty, with arms as the only means of compulsion, follows Wolff JG § 430 note; Burlamaqui only states Grotius II.15.15's stock rule.

rejudge.label: verbatim
rejudge.reason: Vattel names Grotius and quotes Barbeyrac's Grotius II.15.15 word for word ('tous les articles du traité'); Burlamaqui only repeats the same sentence ('d'un traité').

rejudge.label: verbatim
rejudge.reason: Vattel's clause matches Barbeyrac's Grotius II.15.15 exactly ('ne le rompra point', 'qu'une des parties'), where Burlamaqui differs ('pas entièrement', 'l'une des parties'): Vattel ('Il ajoute') follows Grotius, not Burlamaqui.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Stock doctrine; Vattel's distinction of conventions by subordinate powers under express order or within their office follows Wolff JG § 464, and the wording differs from Burlamaqui's.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Reserved ratification must be express is Grotius II.15.17.2 with Barbeyrac's note 1 ('on entend par là ... une ratification expresse'), closer to Vattel's 'comme cela s'entend' than Burlamaqui is.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Stock rule (Grotius II.15.16.3; Wolff JG §§ 465, 468: sponsio binds only if ratified expressly or tacitly), which Vattel follows; Burlamaqui only states it.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Tacit ratification by acts referable to no other cause is Grotius II.15.17.3 and Wolff JG § 468, which Vattel follows; Burlamaqui repeats the commonplace.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's definition of sponsio translates Wolff JG § 465 ('sine mandato potestatis summae, nec intra fines praepositionis' = 'hors des termes de sa commission, et sans ordre'); Burlamaqui gives the stock Grotian definition in other words.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Wolff JG § 470 (silence alone is no ratification; dissent should be declared as soon as the sovereign learns of the sponsio); Burlamaqui only states the same Grotian point.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's passage (only liberty pledged; hostages kept captive, not killed; killing them an error about a right over life) follows Wolff JG §§ 501, 532; Burlamaqui states the common doctrine.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Hostages free once the engagement is fulfilled is Wolff JG § 502, which Vattel follows; a commonplace in Burlamaqui.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's ground (burdens borne equally by citizens) follows Wolff JG § 536 (obses solus id gratis subire non tenetur); Burlamaqui states indemnity in other words.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui copies Pufendorf VIII.8.6 (Barbeyrac); Vattel's rule with an equivalent substitute and his argument that the treaty did not make the king a hostage follow Wolff JG § 519.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui's reason is Barbeyrac's note 2 to Pufendorf VIII.8.6; Vattel's presumption of the state's non-consent matches Wolff JG § 519 and that note as much as Burlamaqui.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Hostage kept as captive (perpetual captivity) after breach of faith follows Wolff JG § 532; Burlamaqui only states the common rule.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's illicit-case exception is Grotius II.16.26.3 and the tacit just-war clause of alliances Wolff JG §§ 659-660; no aid in a manifestly unjust war is stock doctrine (also Pufendorf VIII.6.14).

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's exceptions follow Grotius II.16.27 (aid not owed when one needs one's forces for one's own defence); Burlamaqui's not perishing with an ally echoes Pufendorf VIII.6.14, a related but general point.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Clear cause and justice first sought is Grotius III.2.5, Wolff JG § 589 and Barbeyrac's note to Pufendorf VIII.6.13, which Burlamaqui follows; 'en venir' is a common idiom, not shared wording.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's first ground (only state to state are citizens' goods the nation's) is Wolff JG §§ 589-590; the reprisals-as-prelude-to-war argument is Barbeyrac's note to Pufendorf VIII.6.13, which Burlamaqui repeats.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's definition of public war translates Wolff JG § 607 ('quod geritur inter gentes, seu auctoribus iis, qui summum imperium habent'); Burlamaqui's sentence is a remark on restricting the word 'guerre'.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Restricting a law-of-nations treatise to public war is a generic scoping remark; 'dont nous avons à traiter ici' is a stock formula and the source passage lacks Vattel's assignment of private war to natural law.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui copies Pufendorf VIII.6.3's division of offensive war; Vattel's three ends (claim, punishment, prevention) follow Wolff JG §§ 615-619.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel translates Wolff JG § 745 ('Bellum publicum sine militibus geri non posse... jus conscribendi militem') and § 747 (droit de majesté); Burlamaqui only states the same inference in a different sentence.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same doctrine, but Vattel's sequence (all bound, unfit excepted, those with useful and necessary functions exempt unless necessity presses, clergy) follows Wolff JG §§ 749-752; Burlamaqui's 'aucun citoyen ne peut s'exempter de prendre les armes' is only a parallel statement.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's definition follows Wolff JG § 621 (justificae from right 'quibus evincitur', suasoriae 'ab utilitate'); Burlamaqui only relays Grotius's raisons justificatives / motifs distinction.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's sentence translates Wolff JG § 619 ('Fines duo priores intenduntur in bello offensivo; tertius in defensivo'); Burlamaqui gives Pufendorf's definition of offensive war (VIII.6.3) almost verbatim.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's concurrence of honest motives with justificative reasons and the justice/prudence pairing follow Wolff JG §§ 621-623; the Burlamaqui passage only states Grotius's distinction.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel naming apparent justificative reasons 'prétextes' follows Wolff JG §§ 624-625 (rationes quasi justificae 'tantummodo praetextus sunt'); Burlamaqui's third kind of unjust war is the common Grotius/Pufendorf classification.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Wolff JG § 629 ('injustum vero est defensivum si offensivum fuerit justum') and § 972; Burlamaqui copies Barbeyrac's note to Pufendorf VIII.6.3 almost word for word, and its sentence form differs from Vattel's.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's argument (nations independent, no judge, so both sides' arms count as legitimate as to effects) is Wolff JG § 888; Burlamaqui shares only Grotius's phrase 'effets extérieurs' (III.6.2), and he applies it to acquiring property, not to doubtful causes.

rejudge.locus: Liv. II ch. I § XI-XII (Des causes de la guerre)
rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's syllogism (war allowed only for injury, so growth of power alone gives no right) is Wolff JG § 640; Burlamaqui, after Grotius II.1.17, only states the same rule.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's declaration as a last attempt to end the dispute without bloodshed is Wolff JG § 710, and 'exposer le sujet' matches Wolff § 740 ('rationes justificae exponuntur'); Burlamaqui's statement of the purpose is generic.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Wolff JG §§ 708-709 (conditional declaration joined to repetitio rerum, no new pure declaration needed); Burlamaqui copies Grotius III.3.7, and its sentence is not shaped like Vattel's.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Publication of war to one's own subjects is in Wolff JG § 737 (publicatio, distinct from denunciatio); Burlamaqui only shares the general point, without Vattel's specifics (dating of rights, effects in the peace treaty).

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Different point: Vattel's 'the nation can only blame itself' if it refuses envoys is Wolff JG § 714 ('qui culpa sua eam reddidit impossibilem'); Burlamaqui says modes of declaration are arbitrary provided the prince cannot be ignorant of it.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's passage on declaring at the frontier and on the aim of the declaration follows Wolff JG § 716 ('non alio fine denunciandum, quam ut pars adversa... bellum avertere possit'); Burlamaqui's statement of the aim is generic.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's § 64 (publication to other powers, 'tel ou tel peuple' = 'cum hac vel ista Gente', manifestos with justificative reasons, orders to subjects) follows Wolff JG §§ 737-740; Burlamaqui's publication to subjects shares only the general idea.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel names Grotius and quotes Grotius-Barbeyrac I.3.4 verbatim, including 'selon le droit des gens' and 'de part et d'autre', which Burlamaqui's copy of the same formula leaves out.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Wolff JG § 728: the thing's nature depends on the owner and not on the place, enemy ships, and the presumption until proof; Burlamaqui gives Grotius III.6.5-6 doctrine only.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's rule (aid to a just war allowed and even owed, none to an unjust one) translates Wolff JG § 656; Burlamaqui, copying Grotius II.25.4, only says one cannot innocently aid a manifestly unjust war.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's ban on alliances with a party to an unjust war, then weighing the good of the state, follows Wolff JG §§ 658-659; Burlamaqui only gives the Grotian commonplace.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: No duty to aid an ally in a manifestly unjust war is common stock (Grotius II.15.13 and II.25.4, Pufendorf VIII.6.14), and Vattel cross-refers to his own §§ 86-89; the two sentences are shaped differently.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui here copies Barbeyrac's note to Pufendorf VIII.6.7; Vattel's two-part impartiality rule also follows Wolff JG § 678 (no troops, arms, supplies) and § 683 ('quod uni praestatur, id praestandum quoque alteri').

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's § 118 (offices owed outside war, access and purchase for both sides' subjects, exception by treaty) follows Wolff JG §§ 683-684; Burlamaqui's 'service d'humanité' rule is Barbeyrac's note to Pufendorf VIII.6.7 copied.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Opposite rules: Burlamaqui (Barbeyrac's note) forbids supplying war goods to either side unless an engagement permits it, while Vattel lets both sides buy everything unless a neutrality treaty forbids war goods, which is Wolff JG § 683 ('nisi expresse aliter conventum').

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same specific rule: in extreme necessity seize a neutral place and restore it as soon as the danger passes, paying the damage (Grotius II.2.10 has no payment); the wording is identical in Barbeyrac's note to Pufendorf VIII.6.7, which Burlamaqui copies, so either may be the source.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The equal-treatment rule is common (Wolff JG §§ 683-684, Barbeyrac's note which Burlamaqui copies); Vattel's exception for changed circumstances differs from Burlamaqui's 'raison manifeste' for favours not owed.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Same stock rule that no hostility may be done on neutral soil, which Grotius III.4.8 states; Vattel grounds it in his own territorial-sovereignty principle, and only the phrase 'aucun acte d'hostilité' is shared.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui restates Grotius's first rule (III.1.2); Vattel's end-justifies-necessary-means wording follows Wolff, Jus gentium § 613.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The Leonidas sentence is Barbeyrac's Grotius III.4.18 word for word, which Burlamaqui copies; Vattel's Justin reference is Grotius's marginal note, and he follows Grotius through the whole section.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Grotius III.4.15, which he cites in the same sentence ('Il est de l'intérêt commun des Nations, qu'on ne donne point de tels exemples'); Burlamaqui only copies it.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The Scaevola praise and Vattel's references (Livy, Cicero, Valerius Maximus) come from Grotius III.4.18; Burlamaqui only abridges the same sentence.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's weaken-the-enemy, strengthen-ourselves argument follows Wolff § 823; Burlamaqui copies Pufendorf VIII.6.17 on keeping captured goods up to the debt and war costs, which is stock doctrine.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui copies Pufendorf VIII.6.18 (booty belongs first to the sovereign); Vattel's reasons (soldiers and auxiliaries are his instruments) follow Wolff §§ 852-854, and the wording is not close.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Sparing temples, public buildings and tombs that do not weaken the enemy is Grotius III.12.5-7, which Vattel cites in the same paragraph (Belisarius); Burlamaqui only condenses it.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's rule that needless hostility is 'licence' echoes Wolff § 926; Burlamaqui only restates Grotius's general rule from the other side.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's 'tout lien d'humanité est rompu' is Barbeyrac's phrase (note 11 on Grotius III.4.18), and 'men remain men' is Grotius III.19.1; Burlamaqui states the same doctrine in other words.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's 'mettre des bornes à ses fureurs ... ses maux n'auroient plus de bornes' follows Barbeyrac's note 3 on Pufendorf VIII.7.2, and the capitulating towns follow Grotius III.19.1; Burlamaqui only states the common-interest doctrine.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui copies Grotius III.1.20 on the Romans; Vattel draws the Romans, the time-and-place custom, Achilles and Livy on Perseus all from Grotius III.1.20 and its notes, and his wording is not close.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: That ruses without perfidy are lawful is common doctrine; Vattel's framing follows Wolff, Institutiones § 1203.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's 'comme dans ACHILLES ... confiance dans sa valeur' is Grotius III.1.20 n. 1 ('la confiance qu'il avoit en sa valeur & en ses forces'); Burlamaqui only abridges Grotius's main text.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The phrase is Barbeyrac's note 11 on Grotius III.4.18 ('c'est les porter positivement & directement à commettre un crime abominable'), which Burlamaqui copies and Vattel follows throughout § 180.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: 'Autre chose est, quand on ne fait que profiter de l'occasion' is Barbeyrac's note 11 on Grotius III.4.18, which Burlamaqui copies and Vattel follows.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Keeping captured goods as the equivalent of the debt and costs is Grotius III.6.1 and Pufendorf VIII.6.17, which Burlamaqui copies; Vattel's punishment clause and expletio juris follow Grotius and Wolff.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Only the stock phrase 'frais de la guerre' is shared; the measure (debt, costs, security) is Pufendorf VIII.6.17, which Burlamaqui copies.

rejudge.label: verbatim
rejudge.reason: Vattel names Grotius and cites III.6.3 n. 7 for Lierre, and his wording ('pendant vingt-quatre heures', 'de l'ennemi') follows Barbeyrac's Grotius rather than Burlamaqui's copy of it.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The clause 'until renounced by a peace treaty' is Pufendorf VIII.6.17 (Burlamaqui copies it), but there it says acquisition is valid against a neutral, while Vattel says a neutral cannot acquire safely, so the argument differs.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel's 'particuliere, ou universelle' follows Wolff § 930, and the split by places and by kinds of hostility follows Barbeyrac's note on Grotius III.21.6; Burlamaqui says 'générale' and covers only places.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Vattel follows Wolff § 934 (fides induciarum non violatur; the culprit punished and goods restored); Burlamaqui copies Grotius III.21.13.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui's two-part rule is Grotius III.21.5 nearly verbatim; Vattel's 'incessamment publier' follows Wolff § 919.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: The rule 'chez soi, tout ce qu'il seroit en droit de faire en pleine paix', with the extra reason from continued war and the list of acts, is Wolff §§ 926-927 (cf. Grotius III.21.7); Burlamaqui shares only the phrasing.

rejudge.label: loose paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui copies Grotius III.21.8.3; Vattel's test (abandonment means the enemy no longer wants the place; signs that he keeps his claim) follows Wolff § 924.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui copies Grotius III.21.6 (with the 'train' proviso Vattel lacks); Vattel's rule and its ground (hostilities suspended) follow Wolff JG § 925.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Burlamaqui restates Grotius III.21.9; Vattel's illness case and 'accident they could foresee' follow Wolff JG § 929, his 'à rigueur'/humanity close Grotius § 9.3, against Burlamaqui's 'accident imprévu'.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
rejudge.reason: Stock phrase also in Grotius III.21.3 and Pufendorf VIII.7.7; Vattel's reason (everyone knows the war resumes) follows Wolff JG §§ 916, 929.

rejudge.label: close paraphrase
